lessons.title: It must have been...
lessons.title_uz: O'tmish haqida taxmin: must have, can't have, needn't have
lessons.goal_uz: O'tmishdagi voqealar haqida aniq darajadagi ishonch bilan taxmin qilasiz (must / might / can't have + V3) va keraksiz qilingan ishni needn't have bilan ifodalaysiz.

words.ex: Historians can only speculate about why the city was abandoned.
The village was abandoned in the 1950s.
That's a plausible explanation.
The theory sounds far-fetched.
There is no conclusive evidence.
The excavation revealed ancient coins.
In all likelihood, the fire was an accident.
We can't rule out the possibility of an earthquake.

steps.title: The mystery of the abandoned city
steps.text: When archaeologists began excavating the ruins near the Amu Darya, they found something puzzling: the houses were full of everyday objects — pots, tools, even jewellery. The inhabitants must have left in a hurry; people who move away gradually take their valuables with them. But why? Some researchers have suggested that an invading army might have attacked the city. However, there is no sign of fire or violence, so a military attack can't have been the cause. A more plausible theory is that the river changed its course. If that was the case, the fields would have dried up within a single season, and the people may well have had no choice but to leave. Without written records, nothing is conclusive. In all likelihood, though, it was water — not war — that emptied the city.
steps.uz: Arxeologlar Amudaryo yaqinidagi xarobalarni qazishni boshlaganlarida, jumboqli narsaga duch kelishdi: uylar kundalik buyumlar — idishlar, asboblar, hatto zargarlik buyumlariga to'la edi. Aholi shoshilib ketgan bo'lsa kerak; asta-sekin ko'chib ketadigan odamlar qimmatbaho narsalarini olib ketadi. Lekin nega? Ba'zi tadqiqotchilar shaharga bosqinchi qo'shin hujum qilgan bo'lishi mumkin, deb taxmin qilgan. Biroq yong'in yoki zo'ravonlik izi yo'q, demak harbiy hujum sabab bo'lgan bo'lishi mumkin emas. Ishonarliroq nazariya — daryo o'zanini o'zgartirgan. Agar shunday bo'lgan bo'lsa, dalalar bir mavsum ichida qurib qolgan va odamlarning ketishdan boshqa iloji qolmagan bo'lishi juda mumkin. Yozma manbalarsiz hech narsa qat'iy emas. Ammo katta ehtimol bilan shaharni urush emas, suv bo'shatgan.

steps.q: Why do researchers believe the inhabitants left in a hurry?
steps.explain_uz: "people who move away gradually take their valuables with them".

steps.q: Why does the writer reject the theory of an attack?
options: There is no sign of fire or violence.
The city had a strong army.
steps.explain_uz: "there is no sign of fire or violence, so a military attack can't have been the cause".

steps.body_uz:
O'tmish haqida taxmin: **modal + have + V3**. Modal tanlovi — **qanchalik ishonchingiz** borligini ko'rsatadi.
**must have** (~95%, mantiqiy xulosa): They **must have left** in a hurry.
**may well have / probably** (~70%): They **may well have had** no choice.
**might / may / could have** (~40%, imkoniyat): An army **might have attacked**.
**can't / couldn't have** (~0%, mantiqan imkonsiz): It **can't have been** an attack.
Xato: "mustn't have" taxmin uchun ishlatilmaydi — inkor mantiqiy xulosa **can't have**!
**could have** yana bir ma'no: amalga oshmagan imkoniyat — You **could have told** me! (Aytsangiz bo'lardi-ku!)
**needn't have + V3** — ish **qilingan**, lekin keraksiz edi: I **needn't have brought** an umbrella (olib keldim, yomg'ir yog'madi).
**didn't need to + fe'l** — kerak emas edi (ko'pincha qilinmagan): I **didn't need to** bring one, so I didn't.

examples.en: You must have been exhausted after such a long flight.
examples.uz: Shunday uzoq parvozdan keyin juda charchagan bo'lsangiz kerak.

examples.en: She can't have seen my message — she would have replied.
examples.uz: U xabarimni ko'rgan bo'lishi mumkin emas — aks holda javob yozardi.

We needn't have cooked so much — half the guests didn't come.
examples.uz: Shuncha ko'p ovqat pishirmasak ham bo'lardi — mehmonlarning yarmi kelmadi.

steps.prompt_uz: Sirli bir vaziyatni tasavvur qiling (masalan: ertalab ofisga keldingiz — eshik ochiq, kompyuter yoniq, hech kim yo'q). Nima bo'lgan bo'lishi mumkinligi haqida 120+ so'z yozing: must / might / may well / can't have va kamida bitta needn't have ishlating.
steps.prompt: You arrive at the office one morning: the door is open, a computer is on, and a cup of coffee is still warm, but nobody is there. Speculate about what might have happened.
steps.example: When I arrived at the office this morning, the door was wide open and the lights were on, but there was nobody inside. Someone must have been there very recently, because a cup of coffee on Aziz's desk was still warm. It can't have been a burglar — nothing was missing, and a thief would hardly have stopped to make coffee. In all likelihood, Aziz had come in early and then rushed out for some reason. He may well have received an urgent call; his phone charger was still plugged in, which suggests he left in a hurry. He might even have gone to help his sister, who is expecting a baby. Twenty minutes later he walked in, smiling, with a box of pastries — he had simply popped out to the bakery. I needn't have worried at all.

lessons.title: Formal or informal?
lessons.goal_uz: Bir xil fikrni vaziyatga qarab rasmiy yoki norasmiy uslubda ifodalaysiz: frazali fe'l ↔ lotincha fe'l, to'g'ridan-to'g'ri ↔ yumshatilgan so'rov.

words.ex: The register of an email depends on the reader.
I am writing to enquire about the position.
The meeting has been postponed.
The ceremony will commence at noon.
Regrettably, we are unable to offer you a place.
Please convey my thanks to your team.
"Gonna" is too colloquial for an essay.

steps.title: One message, two registers
steps.text:
Message to a friend:
Hey Sam! Bad news — they've put off the conference till March, so I won't be coming over next week after all. Gutted! Can you let the others know? I'll sort out a new date once I hear back from them. Speak soon!

Email to a conference organiser:
Dear Ms Clarke,
Thank you for informing me that the conference has been postponed until March. Regrettably, this means I will no longer be able to travel to London next week as planned. I would be grateful if you could convey my apologies to the panel. I will confirm my availability for the new date as soon as I receive further details.
Yours sincerely,
Nodira Yusupova
steps.uz:
Do'stga xabar:
Salom, Sem! Yomon xabar — konferensiyani martga qoldirishibdi, demak keyingi hafta kelolmayman. Juda xafaman! Boshqalarga aytib qo'ya olasanmi? Ulardan javob olishim bilan yangi sanani hal qilaman. Gaplashamiz!

Konferensiya tashkilotchisiga xat:
Hurmatli Klark xonim,
Konferensiya martga ko'chirilgani haqida xabar berganingiz uchun rahmat. Afsuski, bu rejalashtirilganidek keyingi hafta Londonga bora olmasligimni anglatadi. Hay'atga uzrlarimni yetkazsangiz, minnatdor bo'lardim. Yangi sana bo'yicha batafsil ma'lumot olishim bilan bo'sh vaqtimni tasdiqlayman.
Hurmat bilan,
Nodira Yusupova

steps.q: Which formal word in the email replaces "put off"?
In the email, "I would be grateful if you could convey my apologies" is the formal version of:
options: Can you let the others know?

steps.body_uz:
C2 darajasining belgisi — grammatik to'g'rilik emas, **vaziyatga mos uslub**.
**1. Frazali fe'l → bir so'zli (lotincha) fe'l**: put off → **postpone** · find out → **discover / ascertain** · set up → **establish** · go up → **increase** · look into → **investigate** · ask about → **enquire about** · start → **commence**.
**2. So'rovni yumshatish**: Can you...? → **Could you possibly...?** → **I would be grateful if you could...** → **I would appreciate it if...**
**3. Shaxssiz tuzilmalar**: We made a mistake. → **An error was made.** · You haven't paid. → **Payment has not yet been received.**
**4. Qisqartmalardan qoching**: won't → **will not**, can't → **cannot** (rasmiy yozuvda).
**5. So'zlashuv so'zlari** (gutted, gonna, stuff, a bit, really) rasmiy matnga kirmaydi.
Aksincha ham xato: do'stga "I am writing to enquire..." deb yozish — g'alati va sovuq eshitiladi. IELTS General Task 1'da register alohida baholanadi!

Hi Dilshod! You won't believe it — my boss has just told me I have to go to Samarkand for work next week, so I can't come to Bukhara with you guys. I'm so annoyed! Could you tell the others? Let's sort out another trip in May. Have fun without me!

Dear Sir or Madam,
I am writing regarding my reservation (booking reference BK2047) for a double room from 14 to 17 April. Regrettably, due to unforeseen work commitments, I will be unable to travel on these dates and must therefore cancel the booking. As the cancellation is being made more than seven days in advance, I would be grateful if you could arrange a full refund in accordance with your policy. lessons.title: Slim or skinny?
lessons.goal_uz: Ma'nodosh so'zlarning ijobiy, neytral va salbiy ohangini (connotation) farqlaysiz va fikringizni aynan kerakli ohangda ifodalaysiz.

words.ex: "Cheap" often has a negative connotation.
My grandparents lived a frugal life.
He's too stingy to buy anyone a coffee.
Good managers are assertive but fair.
The salesman was really pushy.
Inquisitive children ask lots of questions.
Our nosy neighbour always watches us.
"Passed away" is a euphemism for "died".

steps.title: Two descriptions of the same person
steps.context_uz: Ikki hamkasb yangi bo'lim boshlig'i haqida gaplashyapti. Ikkalasi bir xil xususiyatlarni ko'rgan, lekin turli so'zlar tanlagan.

lines.en: I really like the new manager. She's confident, assertive, and very economical with the budget.
lines.uz: Yangi boshliq menga juda yoqdi. U o'ziga ishongan, qat'iyatli va byudjetni juda tejamkorlik bilan sarflaydi.

lines.en: Really? I find her arrogant and pushy. And she's stingy — she cancelled the team dinner to save money.
lines.uz: Rostdanmi? Menimcha, u takabbur va surbet. Yana xasis — pul tejash uchun jamoaviy kechki ovqatni bekor qildi.

lines.en: Well, she asks a lot of questions about our projects. I think that shows she's inquisitive.
lines.uz: Lekin u loyihalarimiz haqida ko'p savol beradi. Menimcha, bu uning qiziquvchanligini ko'rsatadi.

lines.en: Or nosy! She wanted to know why I left early on Friday.
lines.uz: Yoki burnini suqadigan! Juma kuni nega erta ketganimni bilmoqchi bo'ldi.

lines.en: Funny, isn't it? We're describing exactly the same behaviour.
lines.uz: Qiziq-a? Biz aynan bir xil xatti-harakatni tasvirlayapmiz.

steps.q: What is Rustam's attitude towards the new manager?
steps.explain_uz: arrogant, pushy, stingy, nosy — hammasi salbiy so'zlar.

steps.q: What is Laylo's main point at the end?
options: Rustam is wrong about the facts.
They see the same behaviour but describe it with different words.

steps.body_uz:
Ko'p ma'nodosh so'zlarning **asosiy ma'nosi bir xil**, lekin **ohangi** (connotation) turlicha. C2 da noto'g'ri ohang — xuddi grammatik xatodek seziladi.
**ijobiy → neytral → salbiy**:
slim → thin → **skinny**
frugal / economical → careful with money → **stingy / mean**
assertive / confident → direct → **pushy / bossy / arrogant**
inquisitive / curious → interested → **nosy**
determined → persistent → **stubborn / obstinate**
youthful → young → **childish / immature**
famous → well-known → **notorious** (yomon ishi bilan mashhur)
**Evfemizmlar** — yoqimsiz narsani yumshatish: died → **passed away** · fired → **let go** · old → **elderly** · poor → **disadvantaged** · fat → **overweight**.
Maslahat: inshoda kimnidir tanqid qilmoqchi bo'lmasangiz, **neytral** so'zni tanlang.

steps.prompt_uz: Bir odamni ikki marta tasvirlang (jami 120+ so'z): avval uni yaxshi ko'radigan kishi nuqtai nazaridan (ijobiy so'zlar), keyin uni yoqtirmaydigan kishi nuqtai nazaridan (salbiy so'zlar). Faktlar bir xil qolsin — faqat so'zlar o'zgarsin.
steps.prompt: Describe the same person twice: first from the point of view of someone who admires them, then from the point of view of someone who dislikes them. Keep the facts the same and change only the vocabulary.
steps.example:
An admirer: My uncle Botir is a remarkable man. He is slim and energetic, and although he is in his sixties, he has a youthful sense of humour. He is frugal — he has driven the same car for twenty years — and he is admirably determined: once he decides to do something, nothing stops him. He is inquisitive, too, always asking guests about their lives.

A critic: Botir is a strange character. He is skinny and restless, and at sixty he still tells childish jokes. He is stingy — he refuses to replace his ancient car — and incredibly stubborn: you can never change his mind. He is also nosy, constantly questioning visitors about their private affairs.
